<a id="payment_method_configuration_details"></a>
### `payment_method_configuration_details`

The `payment_method_configuration_details` attribute supports:

* `id` - ID of the payment method configuration used.
* `parent` - ID of the parent payment method configuration used.

<a id="presentment_details"></a>
### `presentment_details`

The `presentment_details` attribute supports:

* `presentment_amount` - Amount intended to be collected by this payment, denominated in `presentment_currency`.
* `presentment_currency` - Currency presented to the customer during payment.

<a id="shipping_cost"></a>
### `shipping_cost`

The `shipping_cost` attribute supports:

* `amount_subtotal` - Total shipping cost before any discounts or taxes are applied.
* `amount_tax` - Total tax amount applied due to shipping costs. If no tax was applied, defaults to 0.
* `amount_total` - Total shipping cost after discounts and taxes are applied.
* `shipping_rate` - The ID of the ShippingRate for this order.
* `taxes` - The taxes applied to the shipping rate. See [`shipping_cost.taxes`](#shipping_cost.taxes) below.

<a id="shipping_cost.taxes"></a>
### `shipping_cost.taxes`

The `shipping_cost.taxes` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - Amount of tax applied for this rate.
* `rate` - Tax rates can be applied to [invoices](https://docs.stripe.com/invoicing/taxes/tax-rates), [subscriptions](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/taxes/tax-rates) and [Checkout Sessions](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout/use-manual-tax-rates) to collect tax. Related guide: [Tax rates](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/taxes/tax-rates) See [`shipping_cost.taxes.rate`](#shipping_cost.taxes.rate) below.
* `taxability_reason` - The reasoning behind this tax, for example, if the product is tax exempt. The possible values for this field may be extended as new tax rules are supported. Possible values: `customer_exempt`, `not_collecting`, `not_subject_to_tax`, `not_supported`, `portion_product_exempt`, `portion_reduced_rated`, `portion_standard_rated`, `product_exempt`, `product_exempt_holiday`, `proportionally_rated`, `reduced_rated`, `reverse_charge`, `standard_rated`, `taxable_basis_reduced`, `zero_rated`.
* `taxable_amount` - The amount on which tax is calculated, in cents (or local equivalent).

<a id="shipping_cost.taxes.rate"></a>
### `shipping_cost.taxes.rate`

The `shipping_cost.taxes.rate` attribute holds a tax rate, with the attributes of the [`stripe_tax_rate`](../data-sources/tax_rate) data source and `object`, the name of its type.

<a id="total_details"></a>
### `total_details`

The `total_details` attribute supports:

* `amount_discount` - This is the sum of all the discounts.
* `amount_shipping` - This is the sum of all the shipping amounts.
* `amount_tax` - This is the sum of all the tax amounts.
* `breakdown` - See [`total_details.breakdown`](#total_details.breakdown) below.

<a id="total_details.breakdown"></a>
### `total_details.breakdown`

The `total_details.breakdown` attribute supports:

* `discounts` - The aggregated discounts. See [`total_details.breakdown.discounts`](#total_details.breakdown.discounts) below.
* `taxes` - The aggregated tax amounts by rate. See [`total_details.breakdown.taxes`](#total_details.breakdown.taxes) below.

<a id="total_details.breakdown.discounts"></a>
### `total_details.breakdown.discounts`

The `total_details.breakdown.discounts` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - The amount discounted.
* `discount` - A discount represents the actual application of a [coupon](https://docs.stripe.com/api#coupons) or [promotion code](https://docs.stripe.com/api#promotion_codes). It contains information about when the discount began, when it will end, and what it is applied to. Related guide: [Applying discounts to subscriptions](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/discounts) See [`total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount`](#total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount) below.

<a id="total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount"></a>
### `total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount`

The `total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount` attribute supports:

* `checkout_session` - The Checkout session that this coupon is applied to, if it is applied to a particular session in payment mode. Not present for subscription mode.
* `customer` - The ID of the customer associated with this discount.
* `customer_account` - The ID of the account representing the customer associated with this discount.
* `end` - If the coupon has a duration of `repeating`, the date that this discount will end. If the coupon has a duration of `once` or `forever`, this attribute will be null.
* `id` - The ID of the discount object. Discounts can't be fetched by ID. Use `expand[]=discounts` in API calls to expand discount IDs in an array.
* `invoice` - The invoice that the discount's coupon was applied to, if it was applied directly to a particular invoice.
* `invoice_item` - The invoice item `id` (or invoice line item `id` for invoice line items of type='subscription') that the discount's coupon was applied to, if it was applied directly to a particular invoice item or invoice line item.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `discount`.
* `promotion_code` - The promotion code applied to create this discount.
* `source` - See [`total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount.source`](#total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount.source) below.
* `start` - Date that the coupon was applied.
* `subscription` - The subscription that this coupon is applied to, if it is applied to a particular subscription.
* `subscription_item` - The subscription item that this coupon is applied to, if it is applied to a particular subscription item.

<a id="total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount.source"></a>
### `total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount.source`

The `total_details.breakdown.discounts.discount.source` attribute supports:

* `coupon` - The coupon that was redeemed to create this discount.
* `type` - The source type of the discount. Possible values: `coupon`.

<a id="total_details.breakdown.taxes"></a>
### `total_details.breakdown.taxes`

The `total_details.breakdown.taxes` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - Amount of tax applied for this rate.
* `rate` - Tax rates can be applied to [invoices](https://docs.stripe.com/invoicing/taxes/tax-rates), [subscriptions](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/taxes/tax-rates) and [Checkout Sessions](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout/use-manual-tax-rates) to collect tax. Related guide: [Tax rates](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/taxes/tax-rates) See [`total_details.breakdown.taxes.rate`](#total_details.breakdown.taxes.rate) below.
* `taxability_reason` - The reasoning behind this tax, for example, if the product is tax exempt. The possible values for this field may be extended as new tax rules are supported. Possible values: `customer_exempt`, `not_collecting`, `not_subject_to_tax`, `not_supported`, `portion_product_exempt`, `portion_reduced_rated`, `portion_standard_rated`, `product_exempt`, `product_exempt_holiday`, `proportionally_rated`, `reduced_rated`, `reverse_charge`, `standard_rated`, `taxable_basis_reduced`, `zero_rated`.
* `taxable_amount` - The amount on which tax is calculated, in cents (or local equivalent).

<a id="total_details.breakdown.taxes.rate"></a>
### `total_details.breakdown.taxes.rate`

The `total_details.breakdown.taxes.rate` attribute holds a tax rate, with the attributes of the [`stripe_tax_rate`](../data-sources/tax_rate) data source and `object`, the name of its type.

## Timeouts

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Removing from State

To stop managing a checkout session whose destroy is refused, remove it from the state without destroying it. In Terraform 1.7 and later, and OpenTofu 1.10 and later, replace the `resource` block with a [`removed` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/removed) and apply:

```terraform
removed {
  from = stripe_checkout_session.order

  lifecycle {
    destroy = false
  }
}
```

Using `terraform state rm`:

```console
% terraform state rm stripe_checkout_session.order
```

The checkout session stays in the Stripe account. Replacing one with `terraform apply -replace` or `terraform taint` fails in the same way, at apply.

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import a checkout session using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_checkout_session.order
  id = "cs_test_123"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_checkout_session.order
  identity = {
    id = "cs_test_123"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the checkout session.

Using `terraform import`, import a checkout session using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_checkout_session.order cs_test_123
```

~> Stripe does not return `shipping_options.shipping_rate_data`, `customer_update`, `line_items.price_data`, `line_items.tax_rates`, `payment_intent_data`, `payment_method_configuration`, `payment_method_data`, `payment_method_options.blik`, `payment_method_options.crypto`, `payment_method_options.demo_pay`, `payment_method_options.klarna.subscriptions`, `payment_method_options.p24.tos_shown_and_accepted`, `payment_method_options.paypal.risk_correlation_id`, `setup_intent_data` or `subscription_data`, so an imported checkout session has them null: a configuration that sets `shipping_options.shipping_rate_data` plans an update after the import, and one that sets `customer_update`, `line_items.price_data`, `line_items.tax_rates`, `payment_intent_data`, `payment_method_configuration`, `payment_method_data`, `payment_method_options.blik`, `payment_method_options.crypto`, `payment_method_options.demo_pay`, `payment_method_options.klarna.subscriptions`, `payment_method_options.p24.tos_shown_and_accepted`, `payment_method_options.paypal.risk_correlation_id`, `setup_intent_data` or `subscription_data` plans a replacement.
